_comment: MEASURED FITNESS FOR v1.3, kept BESIDE the standard. `standard_hash` covers standard.json's bytes (ba2050578ed0…) and every citation resolves through it, so a measurement taken AFTER v1.3 shipped must not change them — the same reason v1.0's measurement is a sidecar and v1.1's is inside the document. A measurement's home depends on WHEN it was taken. v1.3's in-document `category_fitness` was carried across from v1.2 and was measured on the PRE-rule-D engine; this sidecar supersedes it, and the page says so rather than quietly showing one number over the other.

supersedes_in_document.reason: v1.3's in-document block was carried across from v1.2 unchanged and records the engine as it was before rule D: 162 pass rows, 10 confirmed, 12.78% cluster-adjusted. Rule D disqualifies an MPN that is the storefront's own product object id, which removes two of those ten and the two rows that carried them. The document is not edited; this sidecar is the later measurement.

samples.name: coffee
samples.label: Coffee category sample
samples.description: The same 103 brands, deduplicated on registrable domain before capture, 3 refused by the G-10 applicability predicate with recorded reasons, 100 evaluated — re-executed on the current engine. Reconstructed from the recorded run's own output and required to reproduce it: 972 assertion rows, entry for entry, with every status difference on IDENT-001 and nowhere else.
samples.method: Every one of the 162 pass rows the published measurement audited was individually adjudicated against its FULL untruncated evidence. Those adjudications are carried forward here unchanged; what moved is which rows the engine still passes. Rule D removed 2 of them, both adjudicated as confirmed false positives, so both the numerator AND the denominator fall — a correction that removed only the numerator would flatter the rate. The 95% upper bound is a Poisson upper limit inflated by a design effect for clustering within store (ICC 0.2), because rows from one store share that store's copy conventions.
samples.supersedes: 12.78% over 162 pass rows with 10 confirmed, measured before rule D

defects.evidence: deathwishcoffee.com — CAFFEINE CONTENT: Power Surge Single-Serve Pods contain approximately 210mg of caffeine (20% more than our Dark Roast) based on a standard 6oz serving when brewed following…
defects.why_wrong: The only numbers are a caffeine dose (210mg) and a brewed serving size ("a standard 6oz serving") — both explicitly not the product's own weight or capacity.

defects.evidence: groundsforchange.com — The essential concept is to brew double-strength coffee directly onto ice: What you need Drip cone with filter Equal amounts (by weight) filtered hot water (200-205 degrees) and…
defects.why_wrong: Every quantity in the evidence belongs to a Japanese-iced-coffee brewing recipe (water/ice ounces, 1/4 cup of grounds, 200-205 degrees), not to the product's own size.

defects.evidence: hydrangea.coffee — The farm’s volcanic soils are described as rich in organic matter, while narrow canyons channel warm winds through the surrounding landscape—the feature that gave Brisa Eterna its…
defects.why_wrong: "soils are described as rich in organic matter" is the soil-science sense of the word and makes no claim that the coffee is organic.

The JSON-LD emits "sku":"100754","mpn":"100754" adjacent in the same object -- the mpn is a byte-identical echo of the store-local SKU, which the requirement explicitly excludes, and no gtin field exists.

defects.evidence: blossomcoffeeroasters.com — Dark roasted to perfection, our Cold Brew Blend features a washed single-origin from Guatemala and a natural from Ethiopia, creating the perfect balance between clean and sweet.
defects.why_wrong: The evidence says the opposite of the claim: 'our Cold Brew Blend features a washed single-origin from Guatemala and a natural from Ethiopia' describes a BLEND of two coffees — 'single-origin' modifies one component lot, not this product, which is by construction not single-origin.

defects.evidence: brashcoffee.com — Since 1890, coffee has flourished at Aquiares, where organic soils and abundant rainfall have created an ideal terroir for aromatic coffee.
defects.why_wrong: 'where organic soils and abundant rainfall have created an ideal terroir' uses 'organic' in the soil-science sense (organic matter in the soil at the Aquiares farm) — it makes no organic-certification or organic-coffee claim about this product.

defects.evidence: myalmacoffee.com — For a fun and refreshing cup, try this recipe : 15g medium ground coffee 250ml water at 203°F 1:16.5 ratio From the farmers who nurtured this coffee in Ethiopia to our roasters…
defects.why_wrong: The matched text is a BREWING RECIPE — "try this recipe : 15g medium ground coffee 250ml water at 203F 1:16.5 ratio" — a dose of grounds and a volume of water, not the product's own size; this is the exact excluded class, and the merchant is shown the recipe as proof.

defects.evidence: thewestbean.com — Composed of three single-origin, estate grown beans.
defects.why_wrong: "Composed of three single-origin, estate grown beans" says this product is a BLEND of three separate origins — the term is present but the sentence asserts the opposite of the requirement; the store does not state this coffee is single-origin.

limits: ONE of the three identifier defects survives, and it is not an oversight. `www.stumptowncoffee.com` publishes "sku":"100754","mpn":"100754" — the MPN is a byte copy of the store's own SKU, not of its Shopify object id, so rule D does not reach it. The rule that would (`mpn === sku`) was scored over all 36 MPN-publishing products in the corpus at 0 true positives and 7 false, and the seven are the COMPLIANT case: a brand that manufactures what it sells legitimately uses one string for both. It was deliberately not implemented.

The comparison with the general DTC sample is a FLOOR, not a bound, and the two are NOT audited to the same depth. The general sample now records ZERO confirmed false passes — in the ONE defect class anyone has ever mechanically re-checked. Every other class in it is unexamined, which is precisely the state that produced a published 0.83% before this class was looked at.

The bound covers the engine's false PASSES only. False fails are not in it, and rule D creates them: six real merchants in the captured corpus publish a check-digit-valid GTIN on a Product node the extractor does not select, and are now told they publish no usable identifier (`ENGINE_GAPS` P-12).

provenance.notes: The 103-brand run is deduplicated on registrable domain, and the audit's store count is lower than the run's because 23 storefronts produced no passing row at all. ⚠️ A DUPLICATION IN THE WIDER CORPUS THAT DOES NOT REACH THIS NUMBER, recorded so a future bound does not inherit it: the three snapshot sets this project holds (172 general, 44 coffee, 122 coffee) total 338 files but only 334 registrable domains and 335 distinct product URLs — `onyxcoffeelab.com` and `vervecoffee.com` are the SAME product in the general and coffee sets, and `deathwishcoffee.com` appears at both apex and www within one coffee set. Neither published sample pools across sets and both are internally deduplicated (general: 172 files, 172 domains, 172 URLs; this audit: 77 hosts, 77 domains, 77 URLs), so no figure here moves. Any bound computed over the UNION of the sets must dedupe first: two files of one product are perfectly correlated, not merely clustered, and would inflate n while adding no information.

samples.name: general
samples.label: General DTC sample
samples.description: 172 products over 172 stores captured without regard to category — the shape a broad fitness sweep produces.
samples.method: ⚠️ READ THE ZERO BEFORE READING THE PERCENTAGE. Rule D closed every one of this sample's 21 confirmed false passes, so the count is now 0 over 488 pass rows — and x=0 over an audit that checked ONE class is exactly the epistemic state that produced this project's retired 0.83%. The arithmetic here returns 0.85%, which is 0.83% again to within two hundredths of a point, for the same reason it was wrong the first time: the number estimates what the audit thought to look for, not the error rate. Only the identifier class has ever been mechanically re-checked in this sample. The 507-row read that preceded it looked at every rendered row and found nothing, because the identifier row renders no quote. Every other class here is in exactly that position today.
samples.supersedes: 8.81% (x=21) before rule D, itself correcting 0.83% (x=0) published before the identifier class was checked at all
limits: THIS IS NOT A LOW ERROR RATE. It is zero confirmed in the single defect class anyone has mechanically re-checked, over pass rows whose other classes are unexamined. A general sample also estimates the error rate on copy that looks like the average of every category at once, which is copy no individual merchant writes.

The ratio between this figure and the category figure is NOT a measurement, and with x=0 on this side it is not even a comparison. The two samples are not audited to the same depth: one had every passing row read individually, the other had one class checked by machine.

entry_discrimination._comment: ONE ENTRY, because rule D moved exactly one. The other nine entries' rates are unchanged and are read from the document, where v1.3 published them. IDENT-001's in-document record states in its own words that 94.7368% is a FLOOR because it was measured against the v1.2 wording and 'no run has been made against the v1.3 wording, and no engine change ships with it'. Rule D is that engine change; this is that run. Computed through the shipped `verdictFor` in standards/discrimination.ts.

supersedes.why: It was measured against the v1.2 wording on an engine that did not implement it, and the document declares it a FLOOR in those words. Rule D is the engine change that record says had not shipped; this is the run against the v1.3 wording it says had not been made.

entries.note: Re-measured against the v1.3 wording on an engine that implements it. 74 of 76 adjudicated rows fail, against 72 of 76 before — the two rows that moved are the two whose MPN is the storefront's own product object id. The verdict is unchanged at not_discriminating, and it may still not be acted on as a retirement: it is above the band, and every bias declared on the in-document record still applies.
